metrics.method: Manual pass over all 318 lines of data/chats/hannah-x-altr.jsonl. 'Client questions' = messages from Bells Vale Referral that ask something or report a problem needing a response; her ~80 bare DMCA link posts were counted as one ask per reporting session, not per link. 'Unanswered >24h' = no substantive answer within 24h of the ask (a holding reply such as 'let me check' does not count as an answer); includes 3 that were never answered at all (the paid-promo intro, the Orlando photographer follow-up, and her 7/6 resignation). 'Max team silence' = longest gap between consecutive ALTR-side messages = 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-02, 23 days. 'Promises' = explicit future commitments made by ALTR staff; kept = evidenced as delivered in-chat; lapsed = no evidence of delivery and never mentioned again.

2026-06-15 to 2026-06-23 — an 8-day open invoice dispute where the client is correcting our arithmetic, inside a 5-week-old relationship, across three payment rails. Any one of those alone warrants an owner-level call; all three together in week 3 should have triggered one.

2026-06-26 and 2026-06-28 — the same delivery complaint raised twice in three days ('all those leaks are still up'), with an emoji of distress the first time. A repeated complaint is the clearest pre-churn signal in this entire history and it was answered with 'im on it' and 'let me check on this with the team'.
2026-07-06 — the churn message itself, in plain English, and nobody read it. There was no alert, no owner, no trigger. Four days later two colleagues sent her templates.
2026-07-10 onward — 23 days of zero outbound. Nothing in the system notices a client chat going quiet, so the first person to speak was the one who needed paperwork from her.
